transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

Not necessarily. A buzzing pump means it is being powered, but it can buzz when the impeller is jammed or when water cannot get through a blocked/kinked hose. With a clean filter, the drain pump is a leading suspect, but I would not buy one until those two checks are done. 1. Switch off and unplug it; have towels ready. Remove the filter again and shine a torch into the opening. Gently try to turn the small impeller vanes just behind it with a finger. It should move with slight magnetic ‘steps’, not be solidly jammed, loose, or have broken vanes. Look for a coin, pin, hair grip or fabric caught behind it. 2. Check the drain hose at the back all the way to the standpipe/sink waste: no sharp kink, crushing, or blockage where it enters the plumbing. A blocked household waste can give exactly the same buzz/no-drain symptom. If the impeller is clear and turns normally, and the hose/waste route is clear, yet it only buzzes and no water leaves, the drain pump itself is then the likely failed part. A blockage in the internal sump hose is the remaining alternative and normally needs an engineer to access safely.
did all that. impeller spins totally freely with no resistance, feels like its not connected to anything. torch shows one fin looks snapped. hose and sink waste both clear. so its the pump yeah?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
Yes — on that evidence, the drain pump is very likely faulty and replacement is the sensible next step. A snapped vane plus an impeller that spins completely freely with no magnetic pulsing/resistance suggests the impeller has separated from the pump’s magnetic rotor. It can still buzz, but it will not generate enough flow to drain. The clean filter and clear hose/waste remove the usual external blockage causes. I could not verify an exact parts match from the model reference alone, so use the full rating-plate details when ordering through Hoover/Candy spares or a reputable supplier; do not buy solely by appearance. Replacing a pump involves accessing the underside/front of the machine and disconnecting water hoses and wiring, so if you are not confident with that, book an appliance engineer. Keep the machine unplugged and avoid running further drain attempts until it is repaired.

candidates: Drain pump impeller jammed or drain pump failed (high)
Blocked/kinked drain hose or household waste connection (medium)
Obstruction in the sump hose before the pump (low)
